question: Should OpenClaw permanently adopt this strict one-feature/one-coverage-ID taxonomy and the corresponding `smoke-ci` profile narrowing as its canonical QA evidence contract?
rationale: The patch is internally coherent, but it intentionally changes the repository’s QA measurement vocabulary, feature granularity, and profile eligibility; that semantic policy cannot be selected from tests alone.

options.title: Adopt the canonical QA contract
options.body: Accept exact two-part IDs, scenario-catalog semantic ownership, and the 11-category `smoke-ci` profile after the QA owner verifies the reviewed mappings.

options.title: Keep broader profile semantics
options.body: Ask for a narrower revision that retains the current smoke-profile category scope while applying only the validated ID-format and uniqueness enforcement.

options.title: Split policy from enforcement
options.body: Merge or rework only the mechanical validation after a separate maintainer decision defines the desired coverage and smoke-profile semantics.

recommendation.title: Adopt the canonical QA contract
recommendation.body: Accept exact two-part IDs, scenario-catalog semantic ownership, and the 11-category `smoke-ci` profile after the QA owner verifies the reviewed mappings.

likelyOwner.reason: RomneyDa authored the current QA coverage-contract implementation and can provide the immediate mapping rationale; the actual acceptance remains a maintainer decision.
